mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month signals an easing monetary policy, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% indicates a tightening labor market that typically precedes inflationary pressures and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a weakening consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by at least 1% from the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In early expansion cycles (UNRATE > 4.7%), a month-over-month increase in industrial production above 0.5% signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 0.5% and UNRATE > 4.7%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 1% signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS declines by more than 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS declines by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a deteriorating labor market and economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE rises by at least 0.2pp and INDPRO declines by at least 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation environments (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), a rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong economic output, which supports corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.
